result:
I've reviewed w154 and the verdict is **DONE**: nothing is Critical and nothing needs fixing now. The lint check does fail on one line this commit added, though (first item below).

The work-item's branch is gone, so I reviewed commit `2739c54` on HEAD. It is the same change as `c437cb4`, the commit the implementer listed: only the hash differs, because the merge replayed it after the w134 commits. Its three files are all in the work-item's file set.

**What the change does:** when a round started for a proposal gives an outcome other than `DONE`, `work run` now:
- leaves the proposal's status as it was and makes no transition;
- writes nothing on the proposal, as the 2026-10-25 ruling (reading B) asked;
- commits and pushes the round's directory and log;
- exits with an error naming the round, its directory and its outcome.

This covers r86, r87 and r88, and those three scenarios pass. No file under `features/` changed and no test was removed or weakened; the test changes are additions only. The report claims no allowances and none were needed. The size check found no file over 300 lines.

**Two Minor findings, both triaged as observations:**
- **Lint failure:** ruff rule FURB167 at `tests/scripts/stub_claude.py:182`. The line uses the `re.M` alias, so `tools check --base d12acec` exits 1. Writing `re.MULTILINE` fixes it.
- **Merge before the refusal** (`scripts/supervise_rounds.py:62-73`): a round with a non-`DONE` outcome has its branch merged into the initiative branch before `work run` refuses. A round that faults keeps its branch unmerged. So an apply round that committed some spec edits and then gave `BLOCKED` would leave them on the initiative branch, and the next run would start apply again on top of them. The agent's instructions tell it to leave things as they are when blocked, so nothing does this today. The kept commit's message also says "faulted", which the round wasn't. I found this by reading the code, not with a probe.

**Not verified:** the implementer's full-suite figures (I didn't re-run the suite). Also untested: whether `work run` with no initiative named stops only the affected initiative when one of its rounds gives such an outcome. No scenario covers that case.
